doc.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995

title: Quiet life in Las Vegas with their animals
summary: At home they rarely go out, Joe golfs and listens to music, and they keep two dogs and three cats.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Tell us about life in Las Vegas, where you guys hang out most of the time.

Well life in Las Vegas is surprisingly dull. We’re very quiet when we’re at home. We rarely go out, we’re very apt to sleep in front of television in the evening, like many other people, and when Joe comes home his pleasure is to be home and eat at home and go and play golf if he feels like it or just sit and relax and listen to his music. And so we don’t go out a lot. We hardly ever eat out, and the only things that drag us out are when people like Steve and Edye come to town and we go to one of the hotels where they are and see them, or somebody really special. We just went to see Jack Jones in “Guys and Dolls” just before we came here. And that’s the only thing that takes us out. Otherwise we just sit there with our animals and enjoy the climate.
Yes. How many animals do we have right now?
We just have two dogs and three cats.
Oh, you’re down to a pretty low—
We’re way down, yes. Because I promised Joe that as they left us I would not replace. So I have to be very careful not to overcrowd us.
